beats: Hook: one NVL72 rack weighs about as much as a car (~1.36 t) on a footprint smaller than a desk (0.6 x 1.2 m); office floors are not built for it (slide 20) (line_cluster_rack_balance, line_cluster_rack_floor).
Scale: clusters of 100,000 GPUs (Colossus, 2024); later numbers only if verified (slide 16) (line_cluster_campus).
The chip: H100 -> B200 -> Rubin: more FP8/FP4 FLOPs, memory and bandwidth; Rubin numbers are announcements (slide 17) (line_cluster_chip_trio, line_gpu).

Inside the chip (her words, slide 17): FLOPs come first, memory bandwidth must keep them fed, and HBM capacity decides whether the data sits in the fast pantry or must come from slower storage (line_cluster_pantry_cellar).
The node: 8 GPUs on NVLink, ~900 GB/s each (18 links x 50 GB/s): eight chefs passing bowls across one island (slide 18) (line_cluster_kitchen_island).
Leaving the node: InfiniBand ~50 GB/s per GPU, about 18x slower: a bike between kitchens (slide 18) (line_cluster_kitchen_street).
The pod: an H100 SuperPOD links 32 nodes x 8 = 256 GPUs in one NVLink domain through switches (slide 19) (line_cluster_switchboard).
Rack scale: GB200 NVL72, 72 GPUs as one big virtual GPU, ~5,000 copper cables (slide 20) (line_cluster_cable_weave).
Lesson + pitfall: the network is a ladder of speeds; keep the heavy talk on the fast rungs, or the slowest link sets the pace (line_cluster_stairs). Next: four ways to cut the job (L04-03).
Cover (line_cover_l04_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): from one chip to a city: a graphics card, a server, a rack and a campus of buildings in a row, each step bigger.
